alignments.note: אֲדֹנָ takes its own English word under rule 57; the ASV writes a bare *Lord* here, with no supplied *O* or *the*.
The 1cs suffix of the divine title is lexicalized in the name and the ASV writes no possessive anywhere in it; unrepresented under rule 57.
Imperative; no subject pronoun is written for it.
Paragogic/cohortative he has no English realization; its own unit under rule 32.
The ASV renders the object bare (*hear my voice*), spending no word on the preposition's own relation; unrepresented under rule 40.
Construct noun keeps only its own word.

הָיָה carries the jussive frame *Let ... be*; the volitive framing word joins the verb whose mood it renders under rule 17, and the unit is discontinuous around the subject by rule 25. Head on the lexical predicate word *be*.
Subject noun keeps its own word.
Preposition takes the word written for it under rule 11.
No article morpheme stands in the phrase, so the supplied *the* joins the construct noun's unit under rules 15 and 29.
Nomen rectum takes the chain's *of* under rule 19; unit discontinuous around the possessive by rule 25.

review_notes: The vocative אֲדֹנָי is written without *O* here, so nothing is supplied to its unit under rule 36.
*Let ... be* is read as one volitive copular frame on הָיָה rather than divided between a supplied auxiliary and a copula.
